Definition: from G2095 and G4976; well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble (in rank):--comely, honourable.
BiblicalUsage: euschḗmōn is a plain word for comely, honourable. In Mark 15:43, the text says "an honourable counsellor." In Acts 13:50, the text says "But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe euschḗmōn shows us that leadership is stewardship: holding what God entrusted, for the people He loves. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Crucifixion; Paul's Missionary Journeys; The Burial of Jesus
